text:
Macklin Celebrini is 200 points into his NHL career and still the one reason every Sharks game is worth watching. He had a goal and an assist in Wednesday's shootout loss to Pittsburgh, and the New York Post is already pitching a Matthew Schaefer rivalry. Around him, the rebuild's next wave is arriving: The Hockey Writers calls Ivar Stenberg "the one thing going right for the Sharks," and Michael Misa and Sam Dickinson are getting real minutes.

The team results are where the patience gets tested. San Jose is 8-11-2 and 2-7-1 in its last ten, with 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) overall and 3.9 expected goals allowed an hour. Both ends have been unlucky too: the shooters are about 12.9 goals under their chances, and the goaltending about 11.7 goals worse than the shots deserved, though Yaroslav Askarov was excellent on Wednesday. The penalty kill gives up a full expected goal a game.

The bright spot is clear. Celebrini and Will Smith with Igor Chernyshov have 62% of the chances and a 4-2 edge. The problem is behind them: Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring have been outscored 12-4, and Jacob Trouba with Dickinson 8-5, and the Misa, Stenberg and Kiefer Sherwood line has 34% of the chances.

Our numbers give San Jose a 5% chance at the playoffs. This season is about how fast the kids grow, and on that measure, there's plenty to like.
